name: APS Medical Billing
desc:
Credentialist / Provider Enrollment Specialist | $18.00 - $20.00/hr | Data Entry & Research Heavy, No Phones | 
Industry: Medical Billing / Healthcare Administration

What you are actually doing: managing the paperwork pipeline that keeps doctors legally allowed to practice and bill insurance. That means verifying licenses, tracking DEA expiration dates, processing initial credentialing applications, handling re-credentialing, and making sure over 150 physicians stay compliant at all times. You are not on the phone with patients. You are communicating with physicians, clinic staff, and insurance payers to chase down documents and keep deadlines. 

This is a detail-heavy, deadline-driven, largely independent role. You will not be micromanaged but you will be held accountable for your caseload. APS is described as a busy environment with strong job security and a culture that promotes from within

Realistic Job Overview and responsibilities:
This is a healthcare administrative role focused on enrolling and maintaining healthcare providers with insurance companies, government payers, and healthcare networks. The primary responsibility is ensuring physicians and providers remain properly credentialed and eligible to bill insurance companies.
This is not a customer service or call center role. It is a detail-heavy administrative position involving document collection, provider verification, application processing, deadline tracking, and compliance monitoring.
Daily responsibilities include:
• Processing initial provider credentialing and recredentialing applications
 • Verifying provider licenses, certifications, malpractice insurance, DEA registrations, and other required credentials
 • Communicating with physicians, medical offices, and healthcare organizations to obtain missing documents
 • Monitoring license, DEA, malpractice insurance, and credential expiration dates
 • Maintaining credentialing records for 150+ providers simultaneously
 • Following state, federal, payer, and accreditation requirements
 • Updating databases, spreadsheets, and credentialing systems
 • Managing deadlines and ensuring provider enrollment remains active
 • Reviewing applications for accuracy and completeness
 • Maintaining strict confidentiality and compliance standards
This role is highly administrative, deadline-driven, and detail-oriented. Accuracy is critical because errors can delay provider enrollment and insurance reimbursement.
assessment: Possibly. Many credentialing employers use attention-to-detail, administrative aptitude, typing, or Microsoft Office assessments during hiring

• Medical billing offices
 • Healthcare administration departments

 • Medical practice management
